title: New Hubble image of NGC 2174
caption: Part of the Monkey Head Nebula, NGC 2174, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 2174 · constellation Orion · about 6500 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)

recognition.text: Ranked #63 on ESA/Hubble’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: This colorful region, filled with young stars embedded in bright wisps of gas and dust, belongs to NGC 2174, nicknamed the Monkey Head Nebula, which sits about 6400 light-years away in Orion (the Hunter). Hubble released the image to celebrate its 24th year in orbit.

Young stars and bright clouds go together. Stars form inside clouds of gas and dust, and once they switch on, their energy lights up and sculpts the material around them, giving regions like this their glowing, ragged look.

What sets this view apart is the kind of light used. Hubble imaged this part of the nebula in infrared with its Wide Field Camera 3. Infrared light passes through dust more easily than visible light, so it can show stars and structures that would otherwise be hidden. Hubble had already observed this part of the sky in 2011, so the new image was a return visit.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.97 x 3.97 arcminutes) and distance (6500 light years), the frame spans roughly 7.5 × 7.5 light-years. Its light set out about 6,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This is a near-infrared image from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, taken through Y, J and H filters. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Infrared light is invisible to the eye, so the colors here are a translation of wavelengths we cannot see.
